property.name: Villa San Bernardino
property.heroHeadline: A house on Lake Ypacaraí, where nothing is in a hurry.
property.tagline: Not a house for everyone. For those who understand that real luxury is space, silence, and time returned to you.
property.footerDesc: Private micro-sites for exceptional properties. Presented by appointment, never listed on portals.

paragraphs: Forty-eight kilometres east of Asunción, on the shore of Lake Ypacaraí, San Bernardino is where a small number of Paraguayan families chose to live year-round rather than summer. Lakefront residences here change hands quietly. This is one of them.

Eight hundred square metres built on nearly four thousand of private grounds, minutes from the water and under an hour from the capital. Paraguay places no restriction on foreign ownership of urban property — full freehold title, no residency required.

story.title: What it feels like to arrive
paragraphs: There is a precise moment, just past the gate, when the noise of the world drops away. The drive opens, the trees close behind you, and all that remains is the lake glinting between the trunks. That feeling — of having arrived somewhere few people know — is the first thing this house offers, before you have even stepped inside.

Indoors, the architecture does not set out to impress. It sets out to accompany. Rooms that breathe, light that shifts through the day, and an infinity pool that dissolves the edge between terrace and water. Everything is arranged so that life happens without effort: a dinner that runs long, a morning with nothing in it, an afternoon with nowhere to be.

Eight hundred square metres that read less as a large house than as private territory. Six bedrooms, a gym, and nearly four thousand square metres of grounds: room for every member of the family to have their own, and to receive guests without anyone feeling like a visitor. Built to last, maintained to hand over today.

lifestyle.title: Living in San Bernardino
lifestyle.intro: Forty-eight kilometres from Asunción, San Bernardino stopped being a summer destination some time ago. It is now where a small group of families chose to stay all year.
introParagraphs: Forty-eight kilometres from Asunción, San Bernardino stopped being a summer destination some time ago. It is now where a small group of families chose to stay all year: close to the city when it matters, far from it when it does not.

The setting combines privacy, mature landscape and easy access to everything the town offers. A residential enclave where the pace changes, for those who value quiet without disconnecting from social life and the movement of the lake.
The position allows you to experience Ypacaraí from a more private vantage point, in spaces built around rest, light and the outdoors.

items.title: The lake, five minutes away
items.desc: Sailing, rowing, or simply open horizon each morning. Ypacaraí as a back garden, not a holiday postcard.

items.title: Asunción in an hour
items.desc: The country's financial centre by motorway. Close enough for business, far enough for calm.

items.title: Privacy you can feel
items.desc: Tree-lined roads, discreet entrances, and neighbours who value the same thing: that nobody knows exactly where they live.

items.title: A community, not a development
items.desc: International schools, yacht clubs and a food scene that grew with the town. Minutes away, never crowded.

inversion.titulo: A retreat that holds its value when everything else moves
inversion.descripcion: San Bernardino is one of the few areas in Paraguay that has neither over-developed nor lost its character. Lakefront supply is structurally limited, and demand for private residential land continues to grow.

datos.label: Character of the area
datos.tendencia: No over-development, no loss of identity

plusvalia.descripcion: The structural scarcity of lakefront land and the preserved character of the area are factors that have historically supported the capital appeal of assets of this kind. Specific projections should be assessed through a current market report.

faq.pregunta: Can viewings be arranged from abroad?
faq.respuesta: Yes. Each viewing is prepared with a video call beforehand so that the essentials are covered before you travel, and the visit itself is accompanied throughout. Advisory available in English, Spanish and German.

faq.pregunta: Can a foreign buyer purchase without residency?
faq.respuesta: Yes. Paraguayan law allows foreign individuals and companies to acquire urban property in full freehold, with no residency requirement and no restriction on repatriating proceeds on resale. Independent legal and tax advice is arranged as part of the process.

Partly, and it is negotiable. The kitchen is handed over fully fitted. Some of the living, dining and suite furniture can be included by agreement; the technical specification sets out exactly what is and is not included.

faq.pregunta: What does the purchase process involve?
faq.respuesta: Five stages: profile validation, private viewing, 10% reservation under private contract, legal due diligence and title verification, and public deed. The advisor coordinates with the legal and tax professionals at each stage.

faq.pregunta: What condition is it in, and when is it available?
faq.respuesta: Immediate. The residence is lived in and maintained: no outstanding works, no waiting. Handed over following a deep clean and full preparation of garden and pool.

faq.pregunta: What are the real monthly running costs?
faq.respuesta: Community charges, garden and pool maintenance, and electricity. The breakdown is set out in the running costs section. Municipal taxes are current.
